key_insight: A projectability-guided atomic-orbital Hamiltonian can faithfully compress plane-wave DFT, including nonlocal hybrid-functional effects, into a compact target for deep-learning models.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more scalable electronic-structure prediction by linking plane-wave reference calculations to equivariant neural networks without sacrificing band-structure accuracy.
method: Select high-projectability plane-wave eigenstates and add a few higher-energy states to complete the AO subspace.
Build nonorthogonal AO Hamiltonians directly from selected PW eigenvalues/eigenstates, avoiding an empirical energy shift.
Train equivariant neural networks on the resulting compact PBE and HSE Hamiltonians.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on MoS2 and sodium phases show accurate reproduction of plane-wave bands with smaller AO bases than real-space reconstruction.
watch_item: Performance depends on choosing an adequate projectability threshold and enough supplemental states to preserve the target subspace.
paper_title: Accurately Generalizing Deep-Learning Hamiltonian Methods to Plane-Wave Density Functional Theory
